para:
Once, there lived a farmer and his wife who had a small baby. They also had a pet mongoose that they loved dearly. One day, the farmer's wife had to go to the market. She asked the farmer to watch the baby, but he also had to leave for work in the fields. Thinking the mongoose would protect the child, they left the animal alone in the house with the sleeping baby.
While the baby was asleep, a long, black snake entered the room. It slithered toward the cradle, ready to strike. The brave mongoose saw the danger and immediately attacked the snake. After a long and bloody fight, the mongoose killed the snake and saved the baby.
When the farmer's wife returned, she saw the mongoose waiting for her at the door. Its paws and mouth were covered in blood. Without thinking, she screamed, "You have killed my baby!" In her grief and rage, she threw a heavy basket of grain at the mongoose, killing it instantly.
She rushed inside, only to find the baby sleeping peacefully in the cradle. On the floor next to the cradle lay the dead, torn-up snake. The woman realized her terrible mistake. The mongoose had saved her child, and she had killed her loyal friend because she acted in haste. She sat down and cried, but it was too late to change what she had done.

questions.question: Why did the farmer's wife leave the baby with the mongoose?
options: She didn't like the baby.
She thought the mongoose was a good protector.
She forgot the baby was there.
The farmer told her the mongoose was a trained nanny.

questions.question: What actually happened while the parents were away?
options: The mongoose ate the baby's food.
A snake tried to attack the baby.
The baby ran away into the fields.
The mongoose fell asleep.

questions.question: Why was the mongoose's mouth covered in blood?
options: It had eaten the farmer's dinner.
It had hurt the baby.
It had fought and killed a snake.
It was sick.

questions.question: What caused the mother to kill the mongoose?
options: She was afraid of all animals.
She acted quickly without checking the facts.
The farmer told her to do it.
She wanted a different pet.

questions.question: What is the lesson of this story?
options: Snakes are very dangerous.
Do not act in haste; think before you do something you might regret.
Farmers should never leave their homes.
Mongeese make bad pets.

para:
In a dense forest lived three friends: a crow, a turtle, and a mouse. One day, they met a deer who was being chased by hunters. They invited the deer to join their group, and the four became inseparable. They spent their days talking and eating together in a peaceful clearing near a lake.
One morning, the deer did not return from her walk. The friends were worried. The crow flew high and saw the deer trapped in a hunter’s net. He flew back and told the others. The mouse hopped onto the crow’s back, and the crow flew him to the net. The mouse quickly gnawed through the ropes with his sharp teeth, and the deer was free!
Just then, the turtle arrived, having crawled slowly to help. At that moment, the hunter appeared. The crow flew away, the mouse hid in a hole, and the deer ran into the bushes. But the poor turtle was too slow to escape. The hunter, disappointed to lose the deer, picked up the turtle and tied him up in a bag.
The friends had to act fast. The deer walked out and pretended to be dead near the lake. The crow sat on her head, pretending to peck at her. When the hunter saw the "dead" deer, he dropped the bag with the turtle and ran toward her. As soon as he got close, the crow gave a signal. The deer jumped up and ran away! Meanwhile, the mouse cut the bag open, and the turtle slipped into the water. By the time the hunter returned, the bag was empty.

questions.question: Which animal was the first to be trapped by the hunter?
options: The mouse
The crow
The deer
The turtle

questions.question: How did the mouse get to the location of the trapped deer?
options: He ran through the grass.
He swam across the lake.
He rode on the crow's back.
He followed the hunter.

questions.question: Why did the hunter drop the bag with the turtle inside?
options: He thought the bag was too heavy.
He saw a "dead" deer and wanted to catch it.
He was scared of the crow.
He heard the mouse talking.

questions.question: How did the turtle finally escape?
options: He bit the hunter's hand.
He crawled out when the hunter wasn't looking.
The mouse cut the bag open.
The deer carried him away.

questions.question: What is the theme of this story?
options: Hunters are not very smart.
It is better to be fast than slow.
Teamwork and true friendship can overcome any problem.
Turtles should stay in the water.

para:
A long time ago, a fierce lion named Bhasuraka ruled over a forest. He was very greedy and killed many animals every day, even when he wasn't hungry. The animals held a meeting and told the lion, "Please, if you stop killing us all at once, we will send one animal to your den every day for your meal." The lion agreed, warning that he would kill everyone if an animal didn't arrive on time.
One day, it was a small rabbit's turn. The rabbit was wise and didn't want to die. He walked very slowly toward the lion’s den, thinking of a plan. When he finally arrived, the lion was roaring with hunger and anger. "Why are you so late? And why did they send such a tiny rabbit?" the lion roared.
The rabbit bowed and said, "Sir, it is not my fault. There were five other rabbits with me, but another lion stopped us on the way. He said he was the true king of the forest. He ate the other rabbits, but I escaped to tell you." The lion was furious. "Another king? Show me where he is!"
The rabbit led the lion to a deep well filled with water. "He is hiding inside this fortress," the rabbit whispered. The lion looked into the well and saw his own reflection. He thought it was the other lion. When he roared, the reflection seemed to roar back. In a fit of rage, the lion jumped into the well to attack his rival and drowned. The clever rabbit went back and told the other animals they were finally free.

questions.question: What deal did the animals make with the lion?
options: They would move to a different forest.
They would bring him fruit every day.
They would send one animal a day for him to eat.
They would build him a new palace.

questions.question: Why was the rabbit late arriving at the lion's den?
options: He got lost in the woods.
He was playing with his friends.
He was taking his time to think of a plan.
He was stopped by a hunter.

questions.question: What did the lion see when he looked into the well?
options: A large fish.
The five other rabbits.
His own reflection.
A secret treasure.

questions.question: How did the lion die?
options: The rabbit pushed him.
He jumped into the well and drowned.
He grew too old to hunt.
The other animals attacked him together.

questions.question: What does this story teach us?
options: Being strong is the only way to win.
Never trust a rabbit.
Intelligence and wit are more powerful than physical strength.
Wells are dangerous places for lions.

para:
A hungry jackal was searching for food near a village. Suddenly, a pack of wild dogs began to chase him. To escape, the jackal ran into a dyer’s house and jumped into a large vat of blue dye. When he climbed out, he was blue from head to toe! The dogs didn't recognize him and ran away in fear.
When the jackal returned to the forest, all the animals were terrified. They had never seen a blue creature before. The jackal realized he could use this to his advantage. He stood on a rock and announced, "Do not fear! God has painted me this color and sent me to be your king. I am here to protect you."
The animals, including the lions and tigers, believed him. They brought him the best food and followed his every command. The jackal lived like a king for many weeks. He made sure to keep the other jackals far away from his "court" because he was afraid they would recognize him.
One night, while the "Blue King" was sitting with his subjects, he heard a pack of jackals howling in the distance. Without thinking, he lifted his head and began to howl loudly: "Phoo-waa! Phoo-waa!" The other animals froze. They realized he was just an ordinary jackal who had painted himself blue. Angry at being tricked, the animals chased him out of the forest, and he was never seen again.

questions.question: How did the jackal become blue?
options: He was born that way.
He fell into a vat of dye in a village.
A magician cast a spell on him.
He ate too many blueberries.

questions.question: Why did the other animals make the jackal their king?
options: He was the strongest animal.
They thought he was a special messenger from God.
He promised them a lot of money.
He was very kind to them.

questions.question: What did the jackal do to prevent the animals from finding out his secret?
options: He never spoke to anyone.
He stayed inside a cave all day.
He kept all other jackals away from his court.
He wore a mask at all times.

questions.question: How was the jackal finally caught?
options: The rain washed off the blue dye.
He told a tiger his secret by accident.
He couldn't stop himself from howling like a jackal.
A villager came to the forest looking for him.

questions.question: What is the moral of the story?
options: Blue is a very pretty color.
You cannot hide your true nature for long with lies and trickery.
Jackals are the best singers in the forest.
It is good to be a king.
